findings.claim: The public-field eligibility check is inverted: `public int Value;` is excluded from contractless and surrogate generation, while `public readonly int ReadOnly;` is included and then modelled as writable. Consequently mutable public fields silently lose their serialized data, and readonly fields can make the generated formatter fail compilation with an assignment-to-readonly-field error.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.GeneratedFormatterCollectorReceiptTests.ContractlessGeneration_IncludesMutableFieldsAndSkipsReadOnlyFields. It generates a formatter for a type containing both a public mutable field and a public readonly field, requires successful compilation, and checks that only the mutable field appears in the formatter.

findings.claim: When SurrogateType is null, the collector unconditionally builds contractless string-key members and never examines attributes on T. For a referenced type marked [MessagePackObject] whose Value property has [Key(0)] and whose Ignored property has [IgnoreMember], the generated formatter uses string-key map serialization and includes Ignored instead of honouring the declared integer-key array contract. This violates the requirement that MessagePack attributes on T be honoured.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.GeneratedFormatterCollectorReceiptTests.MessagePackAttributesOnReferencedType_AreHonoured. It compiles ProjectA with [MessagePackObject], [Key(0)], and [IgnoreMember], references its metadata from ProjectB, generates the annotated formatter, and requires WriteArrayHeader and omission of Ignored.
